doc: The RAM floor per build and ISA, in bytes: tools/floor/ram-floor.mjs (legs ram-floor, ram-floor-armv6m, ram-floor-armv8m).
Builds: default, zc (ZERO_COPY=1), lean (LEAN=1), leanzc (LEAN=1 ZERO_COPY=1), full (LEAN=1 ZERO_COPY=1 LEAN_LEVELS=1, the full memory diet).

engine, screens, audio, platform, libc: .data + .bss of the engine and the port by the source file that defines each static (nm -S -l), the measuring harness and the zone arena left out; align: the link's padding in those sections.

zone: the build's play-inclusive zone minimum, zone_kb x 1024 (zone-min.mjs --build <b> --play --scan: <kb> passes, <kb> - 4 fails, every 4 KiB step from <kb> to 92 KiB or more above it passes); every ram-floor run re-runs the play set at it on every ISA.

stack, heap: the peaks over the play set at that zone (x86: below main's frame, and the bytes the engine and port requested; Cortex-M: from the top of the stack region, and newlib's sbrk high-water, which on tnt.wad and plutonia.wad includes the qemu board's 49-50 KB copy of their WAD directory, wad_semi.c).
A copying Cortex-M build (default, lean) is statics only (statics_only says why); its sum is its statics.
tolerance_why: Every part is exact for a given tree and toolchain: statics come from the link, and the stack and heap peaks repeat to the byte (x86 runs on a virtual clock, qemu under -icount; measured: three runs of one scenario with different environments gave the same MEM line).  The zone is not in the tolerance: it is pass or fail at its recorded minimum.  So the tolerance is policy, not noise: 1,024 B lets a few words of new state through without a re-record, and is 0.2% of the RP2350's 520 KB of SRAM, below anything worth a line in a RAM budget (a table, a buffer).  It is measured from the golden, not from the last run, so small rises add up and trip it.

armv6m/default.statics_only: a copying Cortex-M build cannot play the game with its sound here
